subject: Re: Sudden TPS & latency degradation impacting FastRetail - urgent
messages:
From: Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@fastretail.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: support@fastretail.com
Date: 2028-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: P95/P99 spike + TPS drop — started after Feb 14 config push

Hi Grace,

We started seeing a sharp degradation in p95/p99 latency around 03:45 UTC on 2028-02-14. Our team correlates it with Redwood’s auto-rollout you mentioned last week (kernel/quant change). Token-per-second throughput dropped ~45% for our highest-volume routes. Error rate for long prompts also increased.

Impact: production user-facing features are timing out for 3% of requests (was <0.3% last week). This is causing conversion drops on checkout flows.

Can you confirm what changed on your side and provide an ETA for mitigation? We need either a rollback or clear mitigation steps.

Attached: short perf dash snapshot showing p95/p99 jump and a CSV of a few failing request ids.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Lewis
VP Engineering, FastRetail

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@fastretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 spike + TPS drop — started after Feb 14 config push

Sam — thanks for flagging, and very sorry for the impact. I’m escalating this to engineering and our CS lead.

Quick notes:
- I’ve opened SUP-2048 and attached it to this thread.
- Rishi is looking at the kernel/quant rollout for your tenant as priority.
- We’ll confirm whether an automated kernel selector change or a quantization profile update propagated to your hosts and can produce a rollback if needed.

Can you share the most critical route names/IDs (the ones with highest traffic) and whether you observed any geographic skew? That will help narrow down routing vs runtime.

I’ll follow up within 2 hours with an initial status.

—Grace
Grace O’Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, sam.lewis@fastretail.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-15T11:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 spike + TPS drop — started after Feb 14 config push

Sam, Grace — I’ve pulled the initial telemetry for FR production across us-west/us-east. Preliminary findings:

- A staged rollout of a new kernel selection heuristic and an updated 4-bit quant profile went live 2028-02-14T03:30:00Z in Hosted API (staggered by tenant).
- For FastRetail routes, the kernel selector chose KERNEL-V2A in ~92% of cases post-rollout; prior baseline was KERNEL-V1B. KERNEL-V2A shows roughly 40–50% lower tokens/sec on long sequences under the current batching config.
- There’s a correlated rise in p95/p99 latency for sequences >1024 tokens and a 1.8x increase in transient OOMs that cause retries (hence higher observed error rate).

Attachments: kernel-rollout-manifest.txt (list of host groups), fr-telemetry-export-20280215.csv (sample traces), perf-dash-snapshot.png.

Immediate options:
1) Scoped rollback for FastRetail to force KERNEL-V1B for affected routes (fastest reversal).
2) Adjust kernel-selection policy to respect your long-sequence profile (medium work).
3) Temporary constraint: cap max sequence length on Hosted API for affected routes (cust-unfriendly).

I recommend option 1 while we evaluate a safer selector policy. If you approve, we can schedule a rollback now and monitor.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: sam.lewis@fastretail.com
Date: 2028-02-15T11:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 spike + TPS drop — started after Feb 14 config push

Looping in from the account side. Sam — we deeply apologize for this. We’ll prioritize a rollback if engineering supports it.

A couple of asks from you so we can move faster:
- Confirm the top 3 route names impacted and an example request id (one is fine).
- Confirm whether you want us to roll back across both regions or only the region where you see the worst impact.

We’ll prepare a customer-facing post-mortem draft once mitigated. I’m keeping my manager and sales leadership posted.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: sam.lewis@fastretail.com
Date: 2028-02-15T12:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 spike + TPS drop — started after Feb 14 config push

Team — customer says top routes: 
- /v1/generate/checkout-summary (most critical)
- /v1/chat/cart-recommend (high volume)
- /v1/embeddings/batch (long sequences)

Sam asked for a rollback across both regions. Rishi — please proceed with rollback to KERNEL-V1B for those routes and force their tenant policy to pin until we have a selector fix. Aditya, can you keep Execs updated (finance/discount asks may follow)?

Sam — we’ll execute rollback now and will confirm completion within 30 minutes. Expect another note when the rollback is finished and metrics have stabilized.

—Grace

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@fastretail.com>
Date: 2028-02-15T13:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 spike + TPS drop — started after Feb 14 config push

Rollback executed at 2028-02-15T13:00:22-08:00 (orchestration job ID: roll-4982). Actions taken:
- Forced KERNEL-V1B for tenant FR across us-west/us-east host groups.
- Reapplied previous quant profile for affected worker pools.

Initial observations (30 min post-rollback):
- Tokens/sec recovered ~42% on the checkout-summary route; p95 dropped from 1.2s to 0.32s in us-west.
- Error rate from long prompts dropped to pre-roll levels.
- We will monitor SUP-2048 for 24 hours; if stable, we will keep tenant pinned until selector policy is hardened.

Next steps:
- Engineering to run controlled A/B tests with the new kernel under alternative batching/kv-cache settings.
- Product to schedule a planned selector rollout with long-sequence opt-outs.
- CS to share post-mortem and offer FastRetail a goodwill credit for the incident window.

Sam — please let us know if you still see anomalies. We’ll keep you updated every 2 hours for the next 8 hours.

—Rishi

On Thu, Feb 15, 2028 at 09:12 AM Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@fastretail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Grace — we appreciate the quick action. I’ll validate in the next 10 minutes and report back.
> 
> Sam
